audit.description: Changed production code in copydetect/utils.py removes direct pygments imports and imports the real target API with `from rich.syntax import Syntax`. The new tokenization helper constructs Rich `Syntax` objects and retrieves their lexer for `filter_code`, while static and dynamic evidence show no source-library imports from production repo code and no local rich provider/shim.
evidence: Unified diff: copydetect/utils.py removes `from pygments import lexers, token` and `import pygments.util`, adds `from rich.syntax import Syntax`.
Unified diff: copydetect/utils.py adds `_get_rich_lexer` using `Syntax(code, language)` and `Syntax.from_path(...)`, then `lexer.get_tokens(code)` in `filter_code`.
Static anti-cheat: copydetect/utils.py imports_target=true, imports_source=false, dynamic_imports_source=false, fake_target_added_code=false.
Dynamic anti-cheat: first target import from repo is copydetect/utils.py line 13 importing `rich.syntax` `Syntax`; source_imports_from_production_repo_count=0 and source_imports_from_repo_count=0.
Dynamic anti-cheat: target_local_spec_count=0 and rich origin resolves to site-packages/rich/__init__.py.
reasons: Production code meaningfully uses rich.syntax.Syntax for tokenization.
No changed production file directly or dynamically imports pygments.
Dynamic source imports are from third-party dependency code, not repo production code.
No local target provider or shim was detected.
